cards.explanation: The answer is that they all go in search of him. The text says the Philistines "…all went in search of him…" (2 Samuel 5:17). Not a few of them, friends, ALL of them. They heard David had been anointed king over Israel, and the whole crowd came looking.

The answer is stronghold. David learned of the search, and the text says he "…went down to the stronghold." (2 Samuel 5:17). A stronghold is a fortified place built to hold up against attack. Smart spot to be, friends, when a whole nation is looking for you.

The answer is that he asks the LORD what to do. The Philistines were spread out in the Valley of Rephaim, and "…David inquired of the LORD…" (2 Samuel 5:19). When the question was whether to go up against them, he took it straight to God. I know plenty of folks who ask LAST.

The answer is False. There is nothing about staying in the stronghold. The LORD answered, "Go up," and said, "for I will surely deliver the Philistines into your hand." (2 Samuel 5:19). He told David to go AND gave him a promise to go with it, friends.

The answer is the LORD. David says, "Like a bursting flood, the LORD has burst out against my enemies before me." (2 Samuel 5:20). He gives the credit to the LORD, not to himself. Then he named the place Baal-perazim.

The answer is False. The Philistines abandoned their idols, and the text says "…David and his men carried them away." (2 Samuel 5:21). Those idols did not stay put, friends. Left behind by their own people, and then hauled off like a pile of junk.

The answer is False. The same enemy came back to the same valley, but "…David inquired of the LORD…" again (2 Samuel 5:23). He didn't coast on the last win, friends. I once stamped the same shape the same way for years, so I know how tempting a routine is.

The answer is to circle around behind them. The LORD said, "Do not march straight up, but circle around behind them and attack them in front of the balsam trees." (2 Samuel 5:23). Same enemy, friends, but a new plan.

The answer is the sound of marching in the treetops. The LORD said, "As soon as you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees, move quickly…" (2 Samuel 5:24). Think about that, friends. The signal wasn't a horn or a flag. It was a sound up in the branches.

The answer is that the LORD has gone out before him. The LORD said the sound "…will mean that the LORD has gone out before you to strike the camp of the Philistines." (2 Samuel 5:24). The sound was not just a cue to go, friends. It told David the LORD was already out ahead of him.

The answer is True. The text says, "So David did as the LORD had commanded him…" (2 Samuel 5:25). No tweaking and no shortcuts, friends. That's following the recipe exactly, and my own stamping would have blurred half of it.
